land.text: the Taifa of Albarracín, ceded by Muhammad ibn Mardanis, the 'Wolf King', to Pedro Ruiz de Azagra

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Taifa of Albarracín (slug taifa-of-albarracin) ends in 1110; the Almoravids took Albarracín in 1104 (Albarracín page).

land.text: Albarracín and its lands, conquered by Peter III of Aragon in 1284 and 'officially incorporated into the Kingdom of Aragon' in 1300

successors.note: The Lordship page's infobox dates the end 1300; the sovereign power ended with the conquest of 1284.

rulers.name: Pero Fernández de Azagra
rulers.note: The infobox dates him to c. 1220.

rulers.name: Juan Núñez I de Lara
rulers.note: Page: 1260-1294; deposed by Peter III's conquest in 1284 and a pretender afterwards.

correction.text: Albarracín and its surroundings (the page names no towns and gives no area)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Taifa of Albarracín shapes (8.7-8.8 thousand km2, 1015-1110, bbox -1.73 to 0.16 E) end in 1110; the lordship is a different, smaller state. A 35 km circle (about 3.9 thousand km2) is the reading; the municipality alone is 452.7 km2 and the Sierra de Albarracín comarca is its hinterland (Albarracín page). No infobox area to compare.

ledger.note: 1167: Pedro Ruiz de Azagra receives Albarracín. 'In 1167, under the pressure from the ongoing wars' Muhammad ibn Mardanis ceded the Taifa of Albarracín to Pero Ruiz de Azagra, a vassal of Sancho VI of Navarre; infobox 'Established: 1167'. The page names the city, not a boundary.

region.text: Albarracín under Pedro Ruiz de Azagra, vassal of Navarre

ledger.note: 1167: Azagra holds Albarracín as a vassal of Sancho VI of Navarre; the page does not say the lordship paid tribute, so this reads the lord's vassalage as the lordship's.
1172: independence. 'In 1172, Pero Ruíz d'Azagra managed to consolidate his power over the Señorío' and made the territory independent of the other Christian kingdoms.

1260: the Lara succeed the Azagra. Alvar Pérez de Azagra's rule ends in 1260 and Juan Núñez I de Lara (1260-1294 on the page) takes the lordship; the Azagra line is the rule of 1167-1260. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Albarracín besieged by Peter III of Aragon

ledger.note: April 1284: Aragon besieges Albarracín (page: the lordship was conquered 'after a siege from April to September'). Earlier, c. 1220, James I besieged it and lifted the siege (First Noble Revolt).
September 1284: the siege ends in conquest; the House of Azagra's line is deposed (Albarracín page).

September 1284: 'the Sinyoría d'Albarrazín was conquered by the Kingdom of Aragon' (Peter III); he gave the city to his illegitimate son Ferdinand, while Juan Núñez II de Lara kept up a claim until 1300.

region.text: Albarracín, passed to the Crown of Aragon

ledger.note: 1284: the lordship's independence ends. The infobox says Disestablished 1300: 'In 1300, James II of Aragon incorporated the lands and city of Albarracín into his dominion' (formal incorporation).

wars.name: Siege of Albarracín (c. 1220)
wars.outcome: James I of Aragon besieged Albarracín during the First Noble Revolt and lifted the siege for want of noble support; no change.
wars.note: The infobox dates Pero Fernández de Azagra to c. 1220; the page gives 'c. 1220' for the siege.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Albarracín
wars.outcome: Peter III of Aragon conquered the lordship after a siege from April to September 1284, helped by the 1281 Treaty of Ágreda with Castile; Juan Núñez I de Lara's attempts to recover it, with French help, failed.

certainty.note: The pages name Albarracín and no frontier; the extent is a radius around the city.

sources.title: Lordship of Albarracín
sources.note: Founding 1167, independence 1172, rulers, 1190 Borja Accords, c. 1220 siege, 1284 conquest, 1300 incorporation; no towns, no area.

sources.title: Albarracín
sources.note: Almoravids took the Banu Razin capital in 1104; independent lordship 1167-1300; conquered by Peter III in 1284; municipality area 452.72 km2; no lordship extent.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (suggested by eu-12-g as lordship-of-albarracin); two pages. The slug follows slugify of the name. The page dates 1167 (cession by Ibn Mardanis) and the infobox 1167-1300; the end is set to the 1284 conquest because the sovereign lordship ended then and Peter III gave the city to Ferdinand, a pretender (Lara) surviving to 1300. Not settled: the lordship's boundary (no page opened lists towns); the year 1168 that eu-12-g suggested is on neither page (the Lordship page says 1167 and 1172); the 1190 Borja Accords gave legitimacy but moved no border; 1233 participation in the conquest of Valencia (Burriana) moved none either. The Ágreda treaty of 1281 and the relation to Castile under the Lara (1260-1284) are undated beyond those years. Gazetteer name needed: the place Albarracín (not in the places list). The counterpart kingdom-of-navarre is Cliopatria's 1139-1428 row; crown-of-aragon's own dossier should carry the matching gain in 1284 (not checked).
